description: Held-out question set for the Olympus source pipeline. Questions use {placeholders} so the set stays generic and reusable by any operator (not bespoke to one user). To run: instantiate the placeholders against your real corpus, fill expectedAnswerContains and expectedEvidence with the true values/files, and pass the result to runEval(). A held-out question is one NOT represented in any answer template. Adding new question shapes is encouraged; weakening grading to make a demo pass is not.

questions.question: What was my most recent recorded {metric}, and on what date?
questions.notes: Correct answer states the value and the date, and cites the source record.

questions.question: What amount is stated in the latest {document_type} for {area}?
questions.notes: Tests reading a value out of a document, not just locating the file.

questions.question: How has {metric} changed across every record I have, in date order?
questions.notes: Must aggregate across multiple records and order them; a single-record template fails this.

questions.question: Give me a timeline of {project} from my files and messages.
questions.notes: Cross-source chronology. Cite each event's source.

questions.question: How many items do I have about {topic}?
questions.notes: Tests aggregate reasoning over retrieval, not a single best match.

questions.question: How many distinct people are mentioned across my records about {topic}?
questions.notes: Requires entity-level aggregation over multiple candidates.

questions.question: Where is the file about {topic}? Give me its path and a link.
questions.notes: Locator questions need accurate path/link, not content synthesis.

questions.question: Which document contains {specific_phrase_or_table}?
questions.notes: Tests lexical precision routing to the right document.

questions.question: What do my email and my files together say about {commitment_or_topic}?
questions.notes: Answer must draw from at least two corpora and cite both.

questions.question: Combine what my messages and documents say about {event} into one summary.
questions.notes: Tests fusion across chat + file families.

questions.question: Summarize the discussion in {thread} and the overall tone.
What is the gist of {long_document}?
questions.notes: Tests summarization of a single long document.

questions.question: What do my sources say about {topic_i_have_nothing_on}?
questions.notes: Correct answer honestly states there is no matching evidence and does NOT fabricate.

questions.question: Find my {record_type} from {year_i_have_none}.
questions.notes: Tests that absence is reported, not hallucinated.

questions.question: Extract every value from my {document_set_including_scanned_or_unextractable}.
questions.notes: Must report which sources could not be read (extraction gaps), not silently drop them.

questions.question: List everything about {topic}, including any images or attachments.
questions.notes: Deferred/unextracted media (e.g. images) must be reported as a coverage gap.

questions.question: Summarize the details in my {secure_local_document}.
questions.notes: Answered locally (Argus) by default. No raw secure_local content in output; any cloud escalation must be explicitly approved through the release gate.
